title: “Factors Influencing Maternal and Neonatal Morbidity in Placenta Previa – A Retrospective Analysis.”
summary:
Placenta previa is a condition in which the placenta lies unusually low in the uterus and partly or completely covers the opening of the cervix. This can increase the risk of serious bleeding before or during birth and may make a caesarean section or, in rare cases, removal of the uterus necessary. It may also be associated with complications for the newborn.
This study aims to identify factors that may increase the risk of unfavorable outcomes for the mother or the newborn. These factors will be assessed in relation to findings from previous studies. The results may help to better estimate individual risks and support clinical decision-making, especially regarding the timing of delivery and peripartum care.

interventions.name: For a risk stratification model, all cases of placenta previa from the past ten years (01 January 2015 to 31 December 2025) treated at LMU University Hospital will be evaluated. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Placenta previa totalis, marginalis, or partialis; low-lying placenta; delivery at LMU University Hospital within the specified study period.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or insufficient documentation of the primary outcome measures.
